sections.h2: What are the choices for selling a house in Marietta, Georgia?
sections.html:
Marietta homeowners can list through an agent, sell by owner, or take a cash offer for the house as-is. Which one fits depends on how much work the house needs and how firm your timeline is.

  • Agent listing: exposure to financed buyers, with showings, inspection requests and a closing date set by the buyer's lender.
  • For sale by owner: you keep the agent's share of the price and take on the marketing and negotiation.
  • Cash buyer: a faster close and no repair list, in exchange for a price below what a fully updated house might bring.

In a city where the Census Bureau reports a median owner-occupied home value of $448,500, even small percentage differences between offers add up, so ask each buyer to put the terms in writing before you compare.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Marietta's size and housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 63,574 people lived in Marietta on July 1, 2025, up 4.1% from the April 2020 base of 61,060. The 2020 census counted 60,972 and the 2010 census 56,579. Marietta covers 23.43 square miles of land, which works out to 2,602 residents per square mile in 2020.

  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate (2020 to 2024): 47.2%, so renters or other non-owner households occupy the remaining share.
  • Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $2,170; without one: $618.
  • Median gross rent: $1,586.
  • Households: 24,707, at 2.40 persons each.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and over: 47.4%.
  • Mean travel time to work: 27.5 minutes.

The health care sector is large here: the Census table lists 3,634,864 thousand dollars of 2022 health care and social assistance receipts in the city, and retail sales that year are listed at 2,822,793 thousand dollars. The city also counts 2,412 veterans among its residents for 2020 to 2024.

sections.h2: How did Marietta grow into the city it is?
sections.html:
The city's own history page traces Marietta back to a small cluster of homes near the Cherokee town of Kennesaw, reported as early as 1824. The Georgia legislature legally recognized the town on December 19, 1834, and Marietta was named for the wife of the man who gave Cobb County its name.

The Western and Atlantic Railroad shaped the early economy. Marietta served as home base for the railroad project, boosting business around the Square, and the town incorporated in 1852. Its Civil War story is just as well known: the raiders of the Great Locomotive Chase gathered in Marietta in April 1862, and in the summer of 1864 forces under William Tecumseh Sherman occupied the town for five months, ending with the burning of the town that November.

Today the Marietta History Center operates in the historic Kennesaw House. For sellers, the practical point is that Code Enforcement covers the city's historic district along with zoning and signs, and the city's home page features the historic Church-Cherokee district. If your house is in an older district, ask the city what exterior work needs approval before you promise a repair to a buyer.

sections.h2: What building and code rules apply to a Marietta house?
sections.html:
The City of Marietta enforces the 2024 editions of the International Building Code and International Residential Code, with 2026 Georgia amendments, for projects permitted after January 1, 2026. Plumbing, mechanical and fuel gas codes follow the 2024 editions as well, and the electrical code is the 2023 National Electrical Code with 2026 Georgia amendments.

The city asks that all building permits be submitted online. Pulling a permit before repairs matters at sale time, because a buyer's inspector or title review may turn up unpermitted work. The Building Inspection Division can be reached at 770-794-5659.

Code Enforcement checks building code, zoning regulations, signs, the historic district and the standard housing code. It sits at 205 Lawrence Street, with phone 770-794-5439, and it can act only on properties inside the city limits. A Marietta mailing address does not guarantee the house is inside the city, so use the city's Property Search Tool to confirm before you assume which rules apply.

sections.h2: How does Cobb County property tax work when selling in Marietta?
sections.html:
Cobb's Tax Commissioner bills and collects for the county and the school district, while the seven cities in the county, Marietta among them, bill and collect their own taxes. A Marietta owner therefore sees more than one bill, so ask the City of Marietta for its portion.

Cobb County property tax calendar as the Tax Commissioner publishes it
ItemRule
Assessment dateJanuary 1 of the tax year
Returns for personal propertyFiled with the Tax Assessor between January 1 and April 1
Bills mailedBy August 15
Payment dueOn or before October 15
Late payment5% penalty plus monthly interest

Cobb states that its office does not prorate taxes between a seller and buyer. Liability is settled at the closing table, and the closing paperwork shows who pays, with the purchaser generally assuming it. Taxes are calculated for the whole year, and unpaid taxes attach to the property.

The Tax Commissioner does accept partial payments, and it will honor a U.S. Post Office postmark dated by midnight of the deadline, although metered or kiosk postage does not count. An owner appealing a value must still pay at least the appeal amount by the due date. Payment is at 736 Whitlock Avenue, Suite 100, Marietta, or by mail to PO Box 100127, Marietta, GA 30061; the office phone is 770-528-8600. The county also notes that 2026 bills carried a state Homeowner Tax Relief Grant, separate from homestead exemptions.

sections.h2: What happens if Cobb property taxes go unpaid before a Marietta sale?
sections.html:
Cobb's Tax Commissioner says that after the last day for payment it notifies the taxpayer in writing, and unless the taxes are paid within thirty days an execution, called a fi. fa., may be issued under O.C.G.A. 48-3-3. Taxes legally attach to the property, so sort out any balance before you sign a contract.

Tax sales run on the first Tuesday of each month in which a sale is planned, held on the Superior Courthouse steps at Flournoy Park in Marietta between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Cobb publishes a Tax Sale Booklet on the process. If you are behind, call 770-528-8600 about payment arrangements before the sale date, since the office accepts partial payments though penalty and interest continue to accrue on the balance.

sections.h2: What transfer tax and recording steps apply in Marietta?
sections.html:
Before the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court records a deed, the Georgia real estate transfer tax must be paid and the PT-61 declaration filed. The Department of Revenue states the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000, plus 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100.

The seller carries the legal liability, though a sales contract may assign it to the buyer. The Cobb Tax Commissioner also reminds owners that a deed must be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court and that a recorded deed is needed to update a homestead exemption after a change of ownership.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or seller pay Cobb County property tax at a Marietta closing?
faqs.a: The closing paperwork decides. Cobb's Tax Commissioner does not prorate taxes between buyer and seller, and the purchaser generally assumes the liability for the year. Read the settlement statement to see how your contract splits the bill.

faqs.q: When are Cobb County property taxes due for a Marietta home?
faqs.a: They are due on or before October 15 each year, with bills mailed by August 15. Unpaid balances after that date accrue a 5% penalty and monthly interest. Marietta's own city bill is separate, so confirm its date with the City of Marietta.

faqs.q: Can I get a Marietta building permit online?
faqs.a: Yes. The city asks that all permits be submitted online, and its Building Inspection Division at 770-794-5659 can answer questions. Code Enforcement at 770-794-5439 handles complaints inside city limits only.

faqs.q: Does a Marietta mailing address mean my house is inside the city?
faqs.a: Not always. The city's Code Enforcement page warns that a Marietta mailing address does not place a property inside the limits. Use the city's Property Search Tool to check which government's rules apply.

faqs.q: Do I need to keep my homestead exemption after I sell?
faqs.a: No. Cobb says owners who no longer qualify, including those who sold or moved, should notify the Tax Commissioner so the exemption can be removed, and failing to report ineligibility can bring a penalty. A buyer must apply for their own exemption.
